chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah loves the bashful, the forbearing, the chaste, the abstemious.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four qualities Allah loves according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on Forbearance, this hadith links divine love to the cultivation of inner purity and self-restraint, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (character) as a manifestation of faith. The four virtues—bashfulness, forbearance, chastity, and abstemiousness—serve as practical markers for the believer’s spiritual refinement, ensuring that modesty extends beyond physical appearance to encompass moral integrity and restraint from excess.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Loves the bashful one, the forbearing, the chaste, the abstemious (self-denying)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from ‘Amr ibn Shamir from Jabir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Allah certainly loves the living person who is forbearing, maintains chastity and restrains from worldly matters (sins).”’
